items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw5y: Serbia's Aleksandar Vučić, in power for 12 years, conceded defeat to a student-led opposition movement after snap elections drew record turnout. The vote followed two years of protests sparked by a train-station canopy collapse in Novi Sad that killed 16 people and became a symbol of government corruption. His concession marks a major political shift in Serbia.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief now challenging Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, held his final campaign rally before Israel's election, telling supporters "Netanyahu must go home." He has positioned himself as a moderate alternative in the country's first national election since the October 7 attacks, aiming to end Netanyahu's long dominance of Israeli politics.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Health officials are racing to trace how Nigeria's first Ebola case in over a decade emerged, after Switzerland said the patient likely caught the virus in Uganda, contradicting Uganda's claim she travelled to Congo. First detected in DR Congo in May, the outbreak has since spread to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria, making it the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak on record and raising doubts about containment.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckpd: Israel heads into a tightly contested general election, with polls showing the governing coalition and opposition nearly tied and half a million first-time voters set to cast ballots. The vote follows three years of regional war and is energized by new tactics like AI-generated campaign videos. Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, has emerged as a notable challenger to long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, reflecting deep divisions in Israeli society.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Celebrations broke out in Belgrade after Serbia's student-backed opposition movement won a major election victory over Aleksandar Vučić's long-ruling party. The win follows nearly two years of protests sparked by a 2024 railway-station collapse in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o: Lewis Hamilton says he wants to keep racing in Formula One into the early 2030s so he can compete in the first African Grand Prix, set for a new circuit in Rwanda under a 10-year hosting deal. It would mark F1's return to Africa for the first time since 1993, despite criticism of Rwanda's human rights record. The 41-year-old is currently contracted to Ferrari through 2027.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq8e: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home after more than 10 months in exile, greeted by crowds of supporters as she travelled toward Caracas. She had fled in January, shortly before the US seized President Nicolás Maduro and backed his deputy Delcy Rodríguez as interim leader, who later signed an oil deal granting the US favourable terms. Machado's return signals a renewed push by Venezuela's opposition amid a US-influenced political transition.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: Brazil's leftist President Lula da Silva defeated right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a runoff, winning just over 51% of votes after a surprise first-round loss had energized the right. Roughly 64 million Brazilians backed Lula versus 59 million for Bolsonaro, a margin of about 4 million votes - a historic comeback, since no Brazilian leader has previously lost the first round yet won the runoff. The vote also faced allegations of voter suppression.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: A US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns in Guinea-Bissau, funded partly by the CDC and Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation, has been halted after the government denied approval, the lead researcher said. The $3.2 million study had drawn criticism from vaccine experts who argued the money should fund direct vaccination instead. It highlights growing scrutiny of how rich-country institutions test medical interventions on vulnerable populations.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvx2: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX had restricted Ukraine's Starlink satellite internet, accusing Kyiv of violating terms of service by using it for military drone strikes, before service was restored. The dispute followed a broader US-Ukraine row over Kyiv's strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, and came after President Trump said he'd told Musk to "put it back." The episode underscores how reliant Ukraine's military has become on a private company's infrastructure for its operations.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/c: Cyclone Arnab is forecast to make landfall on Andhra Pradesh's coast by October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with winds up to 125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have mobilised disaster-response teams, with Odisha deploying eight ministers to vulnerable districts. Heavy rain also continues in Tamil Nadu from an active northeast monsoon.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/with-an-: Rajkumar Rajbhar, on trial for a 2016 murder in Uttar Pradesh, allegedly faked his own death using AI-generated funeral photos and a goat on a pyre to obtain a death certificate and escape the case.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India's Election Commission has ordered a statewide review of all additions, deletions and corrections made to Uttar Pradesh's voter rolls after its Special Intensive Revision process, covering all 403 assembly constituencies. The move follows detected anomalies in districts like Pilibhit and Azamgarh, and the ECI has also barred computer assistants from processing electoral-roll forms going forward. Divisional commissioners will now supervise the scrutiny.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/h: Historian Romila Thapar, 96, argued at a Delhi memorial lecture that colonial-era historians shaped how Indian history is understood by reducing complex social and political processes to simplified religious narratives. She said this framing continues to feed the Hindutva reading of Indian history today, and lamented that history has taken on an unusually public, contested role in India. Her remarks underscore ongoing debates over how India's past is taught and politicised.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kerala-j: The minor son of a Kerala judge posted in Thrissur fatally rammed a scooter rider with the family's Mercedes-Benz. Police are examining the father's liability as the vehicle's registered owner and considering naming him as an accused.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: An under-construction house collapsed in northeast Delhi's Harsh Vihar, trapping at least two people - reportedly a contractor and his father - under the debris. Fire and rescue teams, including the NDRF, responded after the old ground floor gave way during first-floor construction work. The building's owner has been identified and legal proceedings have begun, though the exact cause remains unclear.

Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar warned private firms of action if they sideline Kannada speakers in hiring, after a woman's viral video alleged Bengaluru IT companies rejected candidates who listed Kannada as their mother tongue while favouring cheaper out-of-state hires. Shivakumar said the government would act against any company found deliberately denying locals opportunities. The episode highlights friction between India's hiring markets and regional-identity politics in a major tech hub.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/c: The depression over the Bay of Bengal is set to intensify into a 'very severe cyclonic storm,' likely the second-most intense on record, with winds between 118-221 kmph. It is expected to make landfall between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha on October 28, worse than last year's Cyclone Montha. Odisha has activated disaster-response machinery, with the chief minister stressing a zero-casualty evacuation goal.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/15-shops: A fire destroyed 15 shops and a hotel in a Jammu market, with losses estimated in crores of rupees. Fire and emergency services responded quickly, but the blaze spread rapidly, gutting the shops within minutes.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Apple Operations India reported ₹650 crore in software-development and global-support revenue in FY26, part of over ₹1,400 crore in total revenue, a sharp jump from the previous year. Manufacturing-support revenue nearly doubled too, pointing to a restructuring of Apple's India operations. The growth suggests Apple is building out its Indian subsidiary into a major global engineering and operations hub, beyond just device assembly.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Senco Gold will acquire a 68% stake in August Jewellery, which runs the online jewellery brand Melorra, for ₹68 crore, funded through fresh equity issuance in multiple tranches by February 2027. Including a related promoter-group purchase, Senco's total stake will reach 79%, making Melorra a subsidiary. The deal fits Senco's digital and omnichannel strategy, pairing Melorra's e-commerce strength with Senco's existing jewellery retail base to target younger consumers.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Fairfax-controlled IIFL Capital hired four senior private bankers from Barclays - Neeraj Pandey, Subir Didwania, Kunal Kapadia and Vivek Makim - to expand its wealth-management business targeting ultra-high-net-worth Indian families and non-resident Indians. The hires, several with decades of Barclays experience, will lead IIFL's domestic wealth unit and its Global Indian division for cross-border assets. The move reflects intensifying competition among Indian wealth managers as global banks restructure their staff.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's largest companies are preparing for Ind AS 118, a new accounting standard that changes how income, expenses and operating profit are classified and reported. Audit committees are already discussing transition plans even as final regulatory rules are still awaited, given the complex system changes required. The overhaul could reshape how investors compare companies' reported profitability once implemented.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Indian markets were set for a muted, negative open on October 26, with GIFT Nifty signalling weakness amid cautious Asian trade and a pending US Fed decision. The Sensex and Nifty had already fallen for four straight sessions, with the Sensex down 2.15% and Nifty down 2.63% over the week, hurt by elevated crude prices, geopolitical concerns and investors turning selective during earnings season.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck87: UK Chancellor John Healey is tightly guarding the details of his upcoming Budget, using compartmentalised access and codenames to prevent leaks after last year's Budget speculation was seen as economically destabilising. The secrecy comes even as UK growth has beaten expectations and the IMF praised Britain for planning to cut borrowing, easing bond-market pressure. The real test will be whether this stronger economic footing holds once the Budget details emerge in January.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: JSW Steel said it has navigated geopolitical uncertainty and cost pressures well, while continuing to invest heavily in capacity as India's steel demand stays strong, aided by an upgraded IMF growth outlook. The company reported an inventory drawdown signalling solid demand, alongside a strengthened balance sheet from internal accruals and debt reduction. Its strategy centres on expanding production and shifting toward higher-value steel products.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: India's consumer regulator CCPA fined Hogar Technologies ₹1 lakh for misleading walkie-talkie advertisements, ruling that such ads must disclose operating frequencies, licensing requirements and other regulatory details so consumers can make informed decisions.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: JSW Group is seeking to raise its stake in JSW MG Motor India even as the venture stays heavily reliant on Chinese partner SAIC, which supplied about 70% of its FY26 purchases worth roughly $840 million including royalty and licence fees. Total JV procurement reached $1.16 billion, with SAIC-linked firms supplying over two-thirds, up from $640 million in FY25, underscoring India's continued dependence on Chinese auto supply chains.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's Competition Commission plans to hire 41 people across departments, including its investigation arm, the director general's office, according to public notices - part of ongoing efforts to build up its regulatory and enforcement capacity.
items.https://inc42.com/features/growth-vs-pro: Swiggy's shares fell about 15% on October 23, wiping out roughly ₹9,000 crore in market value, after Q2 FY27 results showed Instamart's widening losses overshadowing gains in food delivery. Revenue rose 36.1% year-on-year to ₹7,571 crore, and the net loss narrowed to ₹922 crore from ₹1,092 crore a year earlier but widened versus the prior quarter. The results intensify questions about whether Swiggy's heavy quick-commerce investment can ever turn profitable.
items.https://entrackr.com/report/weekly-fundi: Indian startups raised $133.9 million across 15 deals in the week of October 19-24, down sharply from $302.85 million raised by 30 startups the previous week. Growth-stage deals totalled $86.2 million, led by Even Healthcare's $50 million Series B from Khosla Ventures, while early-stage startups raised $47.7 million, topped by AI startup AuxoAI's $20.7 million Series A. The slowdown signals choppier, more selective funding conditions in India's startup ecosystem.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Honasa Consumer promoted Vipul Maheshwari to chief product and technology officer, putting him in charge of product, engineering and analytics. His key task is advancing Honasa's use of AI, including agentic AI that handles multi-step tasks with oversight.
items.https://inc42.com/features/flipkarts-sum: Flipkart has lost 14 senior executives in the past year, with three more VPs departing, amid uncertainty over an IPO and employee stock-option liquidity. Parent Walmart is pushing for profitability even as Flipkart keeps investing heavily in quick commerce and food delivery. The churn among executives who had weathered earlier restructuring suggests deeper strategic tension between growth ambitions and the path to going public.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/unicommer: E-commerce SaaS platform Unicommerce grew Q2 FY27 revenue 15% year-on-year to ₹59.1 crore and net profit 10.7%, with H1 FY27 revenue up 14.7% to ₹110.45 crore. Expenses also rose, with server-hosting costs surging 41.5% and employee costs up 23.4%, pushing total expenses up 18.9%. The steady growth shows demand for e-commerce enablement tools even as rising cloud and staffing costs squeeze margins.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Tender247, an AI-driven platform that simplifies finding government tender opportunities for smaller businesses, has appointed actor Anupam Kher as its brand ambassador, aiming to turn tender intelligence into a competitive advantage for its users.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma scored centuries to help India seal their ODI series against Zimbabwe, while debutant Vaishnavi Sharma took four wickets as Zimbabwe lost by 121 runs.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Manchester United fans sang support for manager Michael Carrick even while jeering the club during a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, United's eighth game without a win and worst run since 2015-16. Carrick's bosses are now in serious talks about his future, but fans made clear their deeper frustration is with the club's broader management, not just the coach. That suggests changing head coach alone won't fix United's problems.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/h: Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma both scored centuries in a record 153-run fifth-wicket stand, powering India to a 121-run win over Zimbabwe and an unassailable 2-0 ODI series lead. India had slipped to 19 for two early on before Pratika Rawal and Harmanpreet rebuilt the innings with a 124-run partnership. Harmanpreet batted steadily while Deepti played the aggressor, sealing a dominant series victory.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Cameron Green's return and several other selection questions are at the centre of debate over who stays and who goes in Australia's squad, as the team weighs its combination ahead of upcoming matches.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/art: Kimi Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix but must wait to clinch his first F1 world title, now leading Mercedes teammate George Russell by 123 points. The 20-year-old Italian beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, and will be crowned champion in Mexico City next week unless he loses more than 23 points to Russell or 24 to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. His dominant form all season puts the title almost beyond his rivals' reach.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/denso-iri: Japan's Denso Iris beat China's Sichuan Yuanda Meile 81-63 to win the FIBA Women's Basketball League Asia final in Bengaluru, relying on collective team play rather than foreign imports. Sichuan, dependent on American Chennedy Carter and Australian Sara Blicavs, struggled after Carter was disqualified early for two technical fouls. Iris built a steady lead through the game, validating a team-first strategy over star-driven rosters.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/25/grok-r: Grok has released the first seven minutes of its AI-generated "Odyssey" series, three months after Elon Musk promised a full-length, historically accurate film version. Musk had criticised Christopher Nolan's own Odyssey adaptation over its casting, positioning Grok's AI version as a rival, though the footage is being described as merely passable rather than artistically compelling. This underlines how far generative AI video still trails traditional practical filmmaking.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: Enterprise AI's competitive edge is shifting from which model a company uses to the "serving harness" built around it - the architecture, memory management and scheduling that determine how reliably and cheaply intelligence gets deployed. As AI moves from experimentation to production, the key question for executives is no longer model capability but delivery at scale and cost, since a fast customer-facing tool needs very different infrastructure than overnight batch processing.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/25/ai-del: Apollo Global Management's chief economist Torsten Slok says AI has delivered "zero financial payoff" to US companies outside the tech sector, with profit margins and revenue per worker flat across the S&P 500 minus the seven largest tech firms. He argues it will be hard for corporate America to convert increasingly cheap AI intelligence into higher revenue growth or margins. The finding challenges the narrative that AI is already lifting productivity broadly across the economy.
items.https://www.theverge.com/column/1017983/: Google's shift toward AI-powered search, especially AI Overviews introduced in 2024, has upended the online publishing industry that long relied on search traffic for readers. Publishers had spent years optimizing pages to rank on Google in exchange for exposure and clicks, but AI-generated summaries now answer queries directly, reducing the need to click through to original sites. The change is forcing publishers to rethink business models built around Google-driven traffic.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/25/the-ho: A wave of AI-powered wearables - pendants, rings and wristbands like Bee, Muse Charm, Plaud and Friend - aim to embed AI into daily life as productivity tools or always-listening companions. Amazon-owned Bee is a $49.99 clip-on device that records surroundings to generate reminders and notes, alongside a pricier Bee Frontier model. Even OpenAI is reportedly building its own compact AI companion device, making wearables a new competitive AI product category.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: BBC's nature series Blue Planet III is deliberately keeping imperfect shots - stray plankton, boats, buoys - that earlier editions would have cut, to prove its footage is genuinely filmed rather than AI-generated. Producer Elizabeth White said the show previously removed such "flaws" to keep images crystal-clear, but overly polished, seamless footage is now itself a giveaway of AI involvement. The approach reflects a broader push by traditional media to visibly signal authenticity as AI-generated content proliferates.
items.https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10: Amazon warned that hackers exploited critical flaws in a widely used programming language - discovered with help from OpenAI and Google AI models - four days before they were publicly disclosed, and the bugs are now being "broadly exploited" worldwide. The US NSA and UK authorities also warned websites were critically exposed, prompting some governments to take sites offline. Undetected for over a decade, the flaws show how AI can both uncover major security weaknesses and speed up their exploitation.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: Celonis chief scientist Devavrat Shah argues enterprise AI needs "decision intelligence" - deep understanding of how a business actually operates - to be useful, since agents risk missing constraints and making costly mistakes without that context. He says AI can support individual tasks within larger decisions, but only if it understands the role each task plays and the surrounding business conditions. The solution starts with connecting AI directly to a company's existing processes and data.

AI infrastructure costs are usually pictured as GPUs and power, but data storage is an overlooked and growing expense, since inference - unlike one-off training runs - generates data continuously with every prompt. Western Digital found that an 8-second AI-generated video clip returned to a user as a 3.97MB file left behind more than 500MB of associated back-end data. Because inference never "retires" the way training does, storage costs compound over time and complicate AI infrastructure budgeting.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Moderators of the r/opensource subreddit introduced new submission rules that ban, among other things, projects built using AI, alongside other new restrictions on who can post there.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/: Google quietly updated its privacy policy, removing a clear pledge that it wouldn't use Gmail, Drive or Photos content for personalised ads, replacing it with vaguer language that opens the door to such use when data is shared across Google services. The change aligns with Google's 2026 "Personal Intelligence" feature, which lets users share data across apps with Google's AI products. The shift suggests the ad-targeting wall around sensitive personal data is eroding as AI features expand.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/intel: The FCC granted Intel a one-year waiver, out of "an abundance of caution," after confusion over a US ban on foreign-made robots threatened to disrupt automated guided vehicles used in its US chip fabs. The robots, often made by Japanese firms like Murata Machinery and Daifuku, move materials around warehouses and factory floors on fixed tracks. The episode shows how broadly worded tech bans aimed at national security can create unintended supply-chain risks for domestic manufacturing.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: A scalable enterprise AI system needs data, engineering, platforms, operating models and governance to work together, according to a session from MIT Technology Review's EmTech Future conference. Vanguard's Jing Wang, who leads its Center for AI & Insights and previously worked at Boston Consulting Group, discussed how a regulated firm like Vanguard builds responsible AI foundations to turn emerging capabilities, including agentic systems, into lasting investor value.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed a law requiring disclosure labels on ads that are significantly modified or generated by AI, covering TV commercials, images, audio and text, regardless of where the ad was produced. It's among the first state laws of its kind, though it carves out exemptions for parody, satire and "evidently fictional" content, terms the law doesn't clearly define. The move could set a template - and loopholes - for other states weighing AI-ad disclosure rules.
